svg.title: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately...

text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/10/27 - Quote - 01

svg.title: A woodland scene accompanies Thoreau's reflection on living with greater intention.

text.tspan: A woodland scene accompanies Thoreau's reflection on living with greater intention.
I went to the woods because I
wished to live deliberately...
Henry David Thoreau (first-person narrator) · Henry David Thoreau · Walden,
Where I Lived, and What I Lived For · Published 1854
In Walden, Thoreau reflects on living beside Walden Pond
in Massachusetts. He describes a simple house and a life
shaped by close observation. In this passage, he explains
what he hoped to learn by moving to the woods. He
wanted to examine what mattered instead of following
familiar routines without thinking. The quotation is an
excerpt from a longer sentence. It presents an experiment
in living, rather than a rule that everyone must move away
from society.
Deliberately means with conscious intention. The place
matters, but the central question is how to live. The ellipsis
shows that the original sentence continues.
Suggest one small change that could help someone live
deliberately without moving to the woods. (Model: They
could set aside time to decide which commitments matter,
rather than accepting every request automatically.)
